correctness.rationale: For each terminal leaf the direct signed Haar kernel has constant mass over every first-divergence sibling subtree; its exact total variation is a scalar path recurrence. The Bellman induction is valid for all states |z|<=1, and yields \(F_h\) exactly. Maximum over atomic rows proves the sharp operator norm, with Bellman sign equality; combinatorial height bounds and a leaf-by-leaf refinement construction prove the exact fixed-N spectrum and comb equality case. The standalone Fraction checker independently verifies 1,275 leaf rows on all 197 plane trees with <=7 leaves; the proof, not enumeration, covers all sizes.

value.rationale: The theorem solves the complete natural spectrum of the unconditional basis constant over all N-dimensional adaptive fair Haar spaces and identifies exact tree-shape extremizers. Pruning to a comb reduces the number of atoms from 2^H to H+1 without reducing worst-case sign amplification, and the fixed-N max/min ratio is asymptotic to \(N/\log_2N\). This is a structural adaptive multiresolution trade-off, not a single small numeric improvement.
